t: (∼(∼p))∧q is equal to
s:
To find the equivalent of the expression (∼(∼p)) ∧ q, we use the Double Negation Law of mathematical logic. 

According to the Double Negation Law, negating a statement twice returns its original truth value, so ∼(∼p) ≡ p.

Substituting this into the given expression:
(∼(∼p)) ∧ q ≡ p ∧ q

Therefore, the statement simplifies directly to p ∧ q.

Options (A), (C), and (D) are incorrect because they inappropriately retain a negation on either p, q, or both, which alters the original truth values.

Correct Answer: (B) p∧q
